messages:
sasha: heads-up — we saw a latency spike on /v1/embeddings around 09:12 UTC when a client sent a 2.5MB payload with mixed dims (512 + 1536). stack traces point to splitter + routing hot path. :eyes:

mike: can you paste the request headers and the splitter logs? curious whether the preflight kicked in or it went straight to the shard.

sasha: logs below (sanitized):
```
INGRESS: tenant=acme req_id=abc123 bytes=2600000 dims=[512,1536] route=default
SPLITTER: decided=no-split (heuristic: prefer dims split only, bytes threshold=4MB)
ROUTER: assigned=shard-17 (dense-slot) queue_depth=2
RUNTIME: batch_time_ms=180 token_ms=2.1 kvcache_lookups=0
```
mike: interesting — splitter considered dims but not bytes. our current heuristic uses bytes threshold=4MB so 2.6MB slipped through. that explains long batch_time for that shard.

jia: that's expected with current config. but note mixed dims can blow up memory of the far shard because kv cache alignment increases pad size. we should consider an early preflight that returns a "split suggestion" to the client when mixed dims+bytes>X.

anne: UX thought: Console should show a per-request preflight hint in the request timeline (like preflight: suggest-split-bytes=1.25MB or suggest-send-dims=1536-first). that way solutions engineers can see why a client was routed one way.

embed-bot: preflight-check: header X-Embed-Dims detected=2, total_bytes=2600000, suggest_split=true, preferred_split=[1536,512], reason="mixed dims + >2MB"

mike: proposal: change preflight threshold to 1.5MB for mixed-dim requests and surface a 422-ish early response with structured hint unless the client opts into "accept-preflight=false". advantages: avoids routing large mixed-dim payloads into single shard, cheaper for runtime. downside: breaks some existing clients who expect opaque success.

jia: +1 but we need a migration plan. maybe canary the preflight for 10% of tenants and add a console toggle per-tenant (enable preflight suggestions). also provide SDK helpers to auto-split on hint.

anne: console toggle + audit log needed. Also a dashboard tile showing preflight hit rate, suggested savings (tokens/latency), and top offending tenants. UX note: make the hint printable in the request inspector, copy-to-curl.

sasha: telemetry: we should emit metrics: embed.preflight.suggested (count), embed.split.applied (count), embed.routing.latency_{split,unsplit} percentile. tag by tenant, dims-pattern, route. This will show net savings.

mike: technically easy. runtime needs a small change: preflight pipeline before routing that returns a lightweight body {split: [[1536,...],[512,...]], reason}. We can reuse existing splitter logic. we also need a header X-Embed-Accept-Preflight: yes/no from client.

jia: SDK change: for python/js SDK we can auto-apply the split if 1) SDK sees suggestion and 2) env var REDWOOD_EMBED_AUTO_SPLIT=true. default off. Add telemetry to SDK to report whether it applied the split.

ops-bot: reminder: any change that alters request shapes needs an internal runbook update. see runbook section "embeddings-ingress".

anne: rollout plan suggestion:
- week1: internal canary (eng-only) with telemetry flag on
- week2: 10% tenants (opt-in via console toggle)
- week3: 50% tenants / SDK opt-in helpers shipped
- week5: default-on for new tenants, existing tenants get 30d notice

mike: open question: what quota semantics change? our billing is per-embedding-unit (dim * vectors). splitting changes how units are counted across requests. we should clarify whether preflight-suggested-split is charge-neutral or billed per actual requests. finance/jira needed.

jia: agree — billing should follow executed requests. preflight hints do not bill. but we need a console meter showing "effective units per user" before/after applied split to illustrate cost savings.

sasha: small API draft for preflight response:
```
HTTP/1.1 206 Preflight-Suggested
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "suggest_split": true,
  "splits": [
    {"dims":1536, "byte_range": [0, 1300000]},
    {"dims":512, "byte_range": [1300001, 2600000]}
  ],
  "reason": "mixed_dims_bytes",
  "estimated_token_ms_saved": 120
}
```

mike: 206 feels ok. prefer we use a 2xx so clients don't treat as failure. 206 is fine though because it's partial. just ensure SDKs don't throw on non-200.

anne: for console telemetry tile show p99_latency for preflighted vs unpreflighted. also surface a histogram of size-by-dim combos. that's useful for product decisions.

sasha: implementation tasks:
- eng-runtime: preflight endpoint + metric emissions (mike)
- eng-platform: console toggle + dashboard (anne)
- devex: SDK helpers + opt-in (jia)
- billing: confirm charge semantics (sasha assign)

mike: I'll draft a small RFC and a canary changelist. target PR by EOD tomorrow.

jia: I'll add SDK stub and a migration doc for client teams. include sample code:
```
# pseudo-js
const resp = await client.embeds.create({data, headers:{'X-Embed-Accept-Preflight':'yes'}})
if (resp.preflight?.suggest_split && process.env.REDWOOD_EMBED_AUTO_SPLIT) {
  const chunks = splitAccordingTo(resp.preflight.splits)
  await client.embeds.create({data:chunks[0]})
  await client.embeds.create({data:chunks[1]})
}
```

anne: ok — +1 to RFC. please cc @support and @finance. also add a sample console notification template for customers when we flip default.

sasha: thanks all. will open RFC and link here. tagging @mike to coordinate the runtime patch. :thumbsup:

mike: noted. starting branch now.

embed-bot: scheduled-telemetry-check: will run daily and post summary in #eng-platform-canary after rollout start.

sasha: end-of-thread: please react with :thumbsup: if you agree with the plan or mention objections.
